title: CLO 2025 Academic Month Practical Combat: 15 Years of Transforming Digital Design
description: CLO 2025 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Now Available! Listen to 3D fashion designer and brand owner Liu Wanting share her learning tips for 3D design and insights from her professional experience.
transcript:
I am very honored to participate in this online academic seminar.  
I will share with you how I transformed from a traditional fashion designer to a 3D digital fashion designer.  
Today's PPT will explain to you from a technical point of view what kind of technical skills we need to support different application products.  
When Mr. Ma was speaking just now, I saw that some of the students were concerned about this issue: when we make digital works, what software do we need to use?  
Today, in this PPT, I will simply share with you.  
I will also explain to you what kind of software we need to master according to different projects and different skill levels.  
Through this introduction, I will help you to establish a concept of digital fashion.  
That is to say, what kind of work effect do I want to achieve in the future?  
In which direction should I work?  
What kind of digital software do I need to learn?  
Please help me to turn to the second page.  

First of all, I will briefly introduce myself to you.  
My name is Liu Wanping.  
I graduated from Dalian University of Art and Design in 2005.  
I am a fashion designer.  
I graduated in 2005 and have been involved in the design and development of fashion products in the clothing industry since 2018.  
In 2018, I started to get in touch with Cloud3D and began my technical transformation.  
Now, I am actually running my own 3D fashion design studio.  
The main content of the studio is also for some enterprises, including some universities and some companies, to provide modeling and design services.  
Then, the faculty will take part in some 3D courses.  
At the same time, I also provide some training to enterprises internally.  
Personally, I also share some of my daily skills and experiences in using software on Xiaohongshu and Bilibili.  
I also want to help those who want to enter this industry and learn this software to grow quickly.  

Since 2018, I have transformed from a traditional designer to a digital fashion designer.  
In 2018, I was in charge of the design and development of the entire product.  
The problem I faced was that the cost of product design and development at that time was very high and the efficiency was very low.  
There was no way to quickly adapt to this kind of fast-changing market.  
So, I wanted to find a kind of fast-changing product that can be used in many different ways.  
So, I wanted to find a solution at that time.  
In the process of finding a solution, I came into contact with Cloud3D.  
This is why I started a transformation of my entire design skills.  

Let's look at the second page and the third page.  
You can see that I have summarized this timeline from 2018 to…  
Please turn to the top page.  
From 2018 to 2015, for the entire seven years,  
the bottom of the timeline is based on what I have participated in and some of the projects I have been involved in.  
These projects all use our 3D fashion technology to participate in them.  
So, the content of the projects covers from solving traditional fashion design to the future,  
in the marketing section, to the customer side, the C-end,  
to carry out virtual fashion display and pre-sale.  
So, it covers the entire industry chain, from development to mid-end sales.  
In fact, all the sections are involved.  
So, in the upper half of this timeline, there are more projects that I have participated in across the industry.  
For example, the 3D modeling that I collaborated on with the Beijing Contemporary Art Museum,  
and then to show some conceptual costumes,  
including selling their own digital products on Xiaohongshu,  
as well as showcasing some of the IP designs of my own in the Yuan Yizhou exhibition.  

Okay, then please turn to the next page.  
On this page, I have listed out, for those who are going to work in the fashion industry in the future,  
whether you are a traditional designer, or a fashion designer yourself,  
we may be at the physical level, communicating with each other online,  
and then everyone on a platform, on the company's platform,  
to complete the design and development of our products.  
This is a simple process of our traditional era.  
Then, with the development of digital technology, including the network,  
now, as a designer, the work content has also changed a little.  
When we have mastered these digital tools, in fact,  
we do not need to be limited to a certain platform, or limited to a certain physical geographical location,  
to carry out collaboration.  
At the same time, the works that we can show can also be more creative,  
breaking through the traditional physical material limitation.  

Okay, let's look at the next page.  
This page is what I actually want to express today.  
So, you can see in the diagram, I have divided the abilities into three levels.  

Let's look at the first level from the bottom.  
If we say that in the future, everyone is going to enter the fashion industry,  
to do design, or to do production, or sales,  
then at this level, in fact, we can master Cloud3D,  
to be able to master all of the main functions of Cloud3D,  
to be able to realize this kind of virtual sample production through Cloud3D,  
and then to involve this virtual sample into our entire development process,  
and then to improve the efficiency of our entire design and development process,  
so that our virtual sample can replace the many physical white samples used in the past.  
At this stage, as long as we master Cloud3D, this one software is enough to meet our daily work needs.  

Then we look at the second ability level.  
When our work scope involves clothing sales,  
we need to show this virtual sample to our sales team,  
to show it to our C-end customers,  
to do pre-sales or customization.  
So in this scenario, for this technical staff,  
the ability to operate software must be stronger.  
So at this point, just knowing how to use Cloud3D may not be enough.  
We need to learn how to use Blender, or CCD, Maya,  
these kinds of traditional 3D modeling software,  
to assist Cloud3D in realizing a combination of different scenarios,  
as well as animation production.  

In addition, to achieve high-end fabric material presentation,  
some students have also asked about this.  
In fact, material presentation is divided into two parts.  
One part is that we can use some scanning equipment  
to capture the material in the real world to create surface texture samples,  
including physical material samples,  
then use equipment to import them into our software for use.  
Another part is that we can use software like Substance 3D, Substance Painter,  
as well as digital 3D drawing software,  
to create digital materials.  
If we want to present more perfect details,  
this kind of software is what we need to learn and master.  

Then we look at the third level.  
If our application scenario is similar to digital art,  
I want to do advertising and marketing,  
and be able to create more dazzling scenes,  
including detailed animation and comprehensive work display,  
then at this time, we will need more 3D software.  
At the same time, because AI technology is becoming more mature,  
AI will assist these 3D software to generate videos, models, and character animations,  
making it more efficient to complete our digital marketing tasks.  

Please turn to the next page.  
So, in the face of different levels, our employment direction has also changed.  
As before, because I have been doing design and research in the traditional clothing industry,  
after my transformation, my actual work scope and the industries I am involved with have also changed.  
I am no longer limited to the clothing industry.  
So, when you have mastered a variety of 3D modeling software and some AI drawing technology,  
you can do cross-industry cooperation.  
For example, you can collaborate with the advertising and marketing industry,  
and collaborate with the CG gaming industry.  

Please turn to the next page.  
Next, I will give you some specific examples of what I have done.  
Then, based on these examples, I will tell you what kind of work we can achieve under different levels of capability,  
what kind of work can be completed, and what kind of effect can be achieved.  

Please turn to the next page.  
This part is what I just described as ability level 1.  
Its main application scene is within the clothing industry, at the design and development threshold.  
We aim to reduce development costs and increase efficiency.  
This is the content of the work.  
What you see here is actually a new series of projects that I proposed according to the client,  
including the color of the fabric.  
Then, according to the fabric they recommended, I provide the style.  
This is the design of the whole series.  
In the past, we might have needed to first draw a picture, then make a white sample, and then make a physical sample.  
After making the sample, we could see the effect of the dress.  
After using the digitalization process, we can say that the whole process is a kind of paperless office.  
That is to say, after I receive the client’s creative plan from the beginning,  
I can directly use Cloud3D on the computer.  
I can use Cloud3D to do a design simulation of the whole series of products.  
After the simulation, I can do a model synthesis through AI.  
At this time, you can basically see the effect of the clothing after it is manufactured.  
Then, when this effect, the synthesis effect of AI appears,  
you can do a style evaluation for internal sales.  
At the same time, if we have our own website,  
we can also put it on the website for the client's pre-sale.  
Then, you can observe the client’s reaction to these styles.  
Through this way, we save the time and materials wasted on production, the whole design, and the entire design development.  

At the same time, this kind of digital sample doesn’t mean that after we finish making a digital version, it will be useless.  
It can actually be accumulated as a basis for our design development for the next season.  
In this way, each season, for example, for classic styles,  
we can make design developments for the next season by simply putting new fabrics into the 3D software to see the effect.  
This also greatly reduces errors in communication.  

In this process, the entire design department’s workflow will undergo major changes.  
In the past, the designer’s work was very important.  
Communication between designers was often a difficult point and where everyone spent more time and energy.  
I personally think that software like Cloud3D applies to our development process by bringing everyone to communicate in one context.  
We all communicate in this 3D interface, which makes everyone’s efficiency much higher.  

Then, let's take a look at the next page.  
This page is called Digital Sample 1.  
It plays a role in the production and manufacturing section.  
This series is actually the Digital Sample 1 that I made for a customer during the epidemic.  
Because during the epidemic, in the past, the factory might have delivered physical samples to the customer for confirmation.  
We would make a series of styles with washing, all made into clothes and sent to the customer.  
During the epidemic, we had to use this kind of online digital sample for confirmation.  
At this time, we shortened the back-and-forth express delivery of Sample 1, including the time cost and material cost of production.  

In fact, the cloud software also provides this kind of industrialized platform.  
We put all the industrial versions of these boards on this platform to evaluate different models corresponding to this platform.  
In fact, this model is very effective.  

Please turn to the next slide.  
So, to summarize our entire technical ability and technical balance:  
At the first level, whether you are a designer or a pattern maker,  
the pattern maker can use this cloud software more quickly because of their own advantage in pattern making.  
So, they can quickly learn to make virtual sample clothes.  
Designers at this level may seem a little tired, meaning they often do not know enough about the craft and modeling.  
If you have a partner who is a design professional, then when you enter the business and digital sample process,  
you will have the ability to make certain improvements at this level.  
With these abilities, you can quickly complete this kind of high-end clothing production.  

Let's turn to the next one.  
Here is a proportion chart of ability.  
You can see that in this proportion, Cloud3D software occupies a relatively large part.  
It can be used for some functional and work needs.  
If we can also design and include some flat software like Photoshop (PS) operations,  
then making this kind of high-end clothing and production will be our production and sales.  

Now, what you see in this series is actually a 3D simulation of clothes and real people for e-commerce detailed display.  
This workflow is because this project was done relatively recently.  
We did this project with Xinyu Productions.  
On this platform, they put all the clothes of the new generation to make virtual clothing.  
The virtual clothing is combined with photos taken by the company.  
All clothing is created for e-commerce.  
The clothing is also a classic style of the past brand.  
But for this year, we may need to change the material and some craftsmanship for pre-sale.  
At this time, we may not need to make real clothes;  
we can directly change the material and put it on e-commerce to carry out a sales test for consumers.  
After the test data is available, we assist the company in making production quantity predictions.  

Please help me to translate to the next slide.  
At this level, we need to face the consumer.  
At this time, we need to use Blender, including PT and SA.  
PT and SA are all kinds of texture-based software.  
You can search online for these software; there are corresponding tutorials.  
At this stage, the designer’s ability to make creative product images is required.  

Please help me to translate to the next slide.  
At this level, we can see that the proportion of Cloud3D is not that large.  
At this time, if you can master Photoshop (PS), Illustrator (AI), and other software,  
you will be able to make a lot of digital art and advertising marketing.  
This part is about digital art and advertising marketing.  
It requires comprehensive 3D software production capability.  
Its main application scene is around 2021-2022.  
Everyone will be able to make digital products for sale.  
This part also includes some digital products I made at that time, including art exhibitions.  
For this part, my application software includes Cloud3D, ZBrush (ZB), Blender, PT, and some other rendering software.  
I also have software that can be used for digital art.  
I also use software like Unity to make digital art more efficient.  
This part is about digital art exhibitions in the future.  
If you want to learn about digital art in the future, I also recommend you learn about digital art.  
I also have some advertising on big screens as well.  
I listed some basic software in the description box.  
If you want to learn digital art, you will need to learn more software.  
If you want to learn digital art, you will need more software.  
If you want to learn about art, I will share with you the production process and software I used in this work.  

Let's look at the process.  
First, I used MidJourney to create a series of concepts based on the concept I created.  
Then, I made the costumes and accessories in Blender.  
Because my character needs to be different from the default model in Clo3D,  
I made the character's hair in a pattern.  
After the pattern is made, it is added to Blender to create scenes, lights, and to show the materials.  
This is the creative process of the art.  

Let's look at case 2.  
Case 2 is a 3D process.  
In order to make the character more realistic, we combined AI to create the model’s face.  
Let's look at the process.  
In addition to the previous process, I made clothes with Clo3D to create scenes in UE5.  
Because UE5 is very realistic in creating scenes.  
At the same time, I also made animations in UE5.  
In the end, I made the model’s face to make the model more realistic.  
Now, after version 7.1, Clo3D has already made the model to create AI faces.  
When I was working, it didn’t have this function yet, so I had to use other AI production tools to make the model look more realistic.  

So, I hope this video can help you understand how to create scenes in UE5.  
Thank you.

chunks.title: CLO 2025 Academic Month Practical Combat: 15 Years of Transforming Digital Design
chunks.content: ## Introduction to Digital Fashion Transformation and Technical Skills This section introduces the speaker's journey from a traditional fashion designer to a 3D digital fashion designer, outlining the essential technical skills and software needed for various digital fashion applications. It addresses common concerns about software requirements and sets the foundation for understanding digital fashion workflows. Liu Wanping, a graduate of Dalian University of Art and Design (2005), transitioned from traditional fashion design to digital fashion design starting in 2018. She began using Cloud3D to improve design efficiency and reduce costs in fashion product development. Currently, she runs a 3D fashion design studio providing modeling and design services to enterprises and universities, along with internal enterprise training. She also shares her software skills and experiences on platforms like Xiaohongshu and Bilibili to help newcomers grow quickly in the industry. Her transformation was driven by the high costs and inefficiencies of traditional fashion design and development processes, which could not keep pace with fast-changing markets. Cloud3D became a key tool in her transition, enabling faster and more flexible product development. --- ## Timeline and Industry Involvement in 3D Fashion Technology This section summarizes Liu Wanping’s seven-year journey (2018-2025) applying 3D fashion technology across the fashion industry, marketing, and customer engagement, highlighting key projects and cross-industry collaborations. Her participation covers the entire fashion industry chain—from traditional design and development to mid-end sales and virtual fashion display. Projects include collaborations with the Beijing Contemporary Art Museum on 3D modeling and conceptual costumes, selling digital products on Xiaohongshu, and exhibiting IP designs at Yuan Yizhou exhibitions. The timeline illustrates a broad involvement in digital fashion, reflecting the integration of 3D technology into multiple facets of the industry and expanding beyond traditional clothing into virtual and digital product showcases. --- ## Evolution of Fashion Design Workflows with Digital Tools This section explains how digital technology has transformed traditional fashion design workflows, enabling remote collaboration, creative freedom beyond physical constraints, and enhanced communication through shared digital platforms. Traditional fashion design involved physical sample development and localized collaboration. With digital tools, designers are no longer bound by geography or specific platforms. Digital collaboration platforms allow multiple stakeholders to work simultaneously on designs, improving efficiency and encouraging more creative and innovative outputs that transcend physical material limitations. --- ## Three Levels of Digital Fashion Design Competency This section defines three competency levels for digital fashion professionals, detailing the software tools and skills required at each level to meet different industry demands from design to digital marketing. ### Level 1: Virtual Sample Production for Design and Development - Mastery of Cloud3D is sufficient. - Focuses on virtual sample production to replace physical white samples. - Improves efficiency and reduces material waste. - Suitable for designers, pattern makers, and production staff in the fashion industry. - Enables paperless workflows and internal design evaluation. - Digital samples can be reused for future seasons by swapping fabrics, reducing communication errors.
chunks.content_description: CLO 2025 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Now Available! Listen to 3D fashion designer and brand owner Liu Wanting share her learning tips for 3D design and insights from her professional experience.

chunks.content: --- ## Three Levels of Digital Fashion Design Competency This section defines three competency levels for digital fashion professionals, detailing the software tools and skills required at each level to meet different industry demands from design to digital marketing. ### Level 1: Virtual Sample Production for Design and Development - Mastery of Cloud3D is sufficient. - Focuses on virtual sample production to replace physical white samples. - Improves efficiency and reduces material waste. - Suitable for designers, pattern makers, and production staff in the fashion industry. - Enables paperless workflows and internal design evaluation. - Digital samples can be reused for future seasons by swapping fabrics, reducing communication errors. ### Level 2: Sales and Marketing Visualization - Requires stronger software skills beyond Cloud3D. - Includes learning Blender, Maya, and Cinema 4D (CCD) for 3D modeling and animation. - Material presentation involves: - Scanning real-world fabric samples to capture textures. - Using Substance 3D Painter and other digital 3D painting software to create digital materials. - Supports pre-sales, customization, and customer-facing presentations. ### Level 3: Digital Art, Advertising, and Advanced Scene Creation - Involves comprehensive 3D software proficiency (Cloud3D, ZBrush, Blender, Unity). - Creates detailed animations, complex scenes, and digital marketing content. - AI technologies assist in generating videos, models, and character animations. - Suitable for cross-industry collaborations including advertising, marketing, and gaming. - Emphasizes creative product image generation and digital art exhibitions. --- ## Changes in Employment Directions and Cross-Industry Opportunities This section discusses how mastering multiple 3D modeling and AI drawing technologies expands professional opportunities beyond the traditional clothing industry into advertising, marketing, and CG gaming. Digital skills enable designers to collaborate across industries, applying their expertise to new fields. This diversification reflects the growing relevance of digital fashion design in various digital content creation sectors. --- ## Practical Examples of Digital Fashion Applications This section provides concrete examples demonstrating the application of digital fashion design skills at different competency levels and the resulting benefits. ### Level 1 Application: Virtual Sample Development in Clothing Industry - Focused on reducing development costs and increasing efficiency. - Example project involved creating a new series based on client fabric recommendations. - Entire design process moved from physical sketches and samples to virtual simulation using Cloud3D. - AI-assisted model synthesis provides realistic previews of finished garments. - Enables style evaluation, internal sales assessment, and client pre-sale feedback. - Saves time, materials, and reduces waste. - Digital samples serve as a design development foundation for future seasons. - Improves communication and collaboration by using a shared 3D interface. ### Digital Sample 1 During the Epidemic - Digital samples replaced physical samples for confirmation during COVID-19 restrictions. - Eliminated the need for back-and-forth express deliveries. - Reduced time and material costs. - Cloud3D's industrial platform supports evaluation and collaboration on digital sample production. --- ## Technical Skill Distribution and Software Usage This section analyzes the software proficiency distribution needed for different roles and projects within digital fashion design.

chunks.content: - Improves communication and collaboration by using a shared 3D interface. ### Digital Sample 1 During the Epidemic - Digital samples replaced physical samples for confirmation during COVID-19 restrictions. - Eliminated the need for back-and-forth express deliveries. - Reduced time and material costs. - Cloud3D's industrial platform supports evaluation and collaboration on digital sample production. --- ## Technical Skill Distribution and Software Usage This section analyzes the software proficiency distribution needed for different roles and projects within digital fashion design. - Pattern makers can quickly adopt Cloud3D due to their craft knowledge. - Designers might require partnerships with pattern makers to improve modeling skills. - Cloud3D occupies a major role in daily work and virtual sample creation. - Photoshop (PS) and Illustrator (AI) complement 3D tools for high-end clothing production and sales. --- ## 3D Simulation for E-commerce and Consumer-Facing Applications This section covers the use of 3D virtual clothing simulations for e-commerce platforms, enabling digital product display and sales testing before physical production. - Collaboration with Xinyu Productions created virtual clothing combined with company photos. - Classic styles updated with new materials and craftsmanship for pre-sale testing. - Eliminates the need for physical samples in sales tests. - Enables data-driven production quantity predictions based on consumer feedback. - Requires advanced software like Blender plus texture software such as PT and SA for creative product imagery. --- ## Advanced Digital Art and Advertising Marketing This section focuses on digital art creation and advertising marketing using comprehensive 3D and digital tools, emphasizing the integration of AI and multiple software platforms. - Use of Photoshop, Illustrator, Cloud3D, ZBrush, Blender, PT, and rendering software. - Application in digital art exhibitions and large-scale advertising displays. - Workflow includes: - Concept generation via MidJourney (AI-powered image generation). - Costume and accessory creation in Blender. - Custom character hair patterns created separately and imported into Blender. - Scene lighting and material presentation in Blender. - Unity software is used to enhance digital art production efficiency. --- ## Case Study: AI-Enhanced 3D Character Modeling and UE5 Integration This section details a case study combining AI technology with 3D fashion design software and Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) for realistic scene creation and animation. - AI used to generate realistic facial models for characters. - Clothing created in Clo3D integrated into UE5 for highly realistic environments. - UE5 employed for scene realism and animation production. - Earlier versions of Clo3D lacked AI face generation; external AI tools were used. - Clo3D version 7.1 now includes built-in AI face creation. - Demonstrates the integration of AI and advanced 3D engines for digital marketing and art projects. --- ## Conclusion Liu Wanping’s experience exemplifies the transformation from traditional fashion design to a digitally augmented workflow involving Cloud3D, Blender, AI technologies, and advanced 3D engines like UE5. Mastery of these tools enables enhanced efficiency, cross-industry collaboration, and innovative digital fashion and marketing applications.
